source_fields.instance: The public nonempty action set X is contained in {0,1}^d, and each action has exactly m active coordinates. The environment fixes z_t in [0,1]^d in advance. After choosing a_t in X, the learner incurs the sum loss <a_t,z_t> and observes the losses of all active coordinates.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public); m: $m\in\mathbb N,\ 1\le m\le d/2$ (public)
interaction_timing: The action space $\mathcal X$ is public; the environment fixes $z_{1:T}$.
The learner selects an admissible combination a_t.
All m active coordinates are observed together. A new combination can be chosen only next round.
source_fields.adversary_information: The environment fixes the entire loss sequence before interaction. It may know the algorithm and public parameters but cannot depend on the learner’s private seed. This is an oblivious-adversary specification and does not automatically extend to history-dependent adaptive adversaries.
unresolved_applicability: Specific action geometries, stronger full-information access, and aggregate-only bandit access require distinct specifications.

operations.query_signature: Inputs: $t,\ a_t\in\mathcal X$. Timing and visible information follow the specified protocol.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: Return exactly $m$ selected coordinate values, from which total loss is computable; unselected coordinates remain hidden. All coordinates in a round belong to the same $z_t$, rather than to $m$ independent online horizons. The action set $\mathcal X$ is public, but no additional unit-cost linear optimization oracle is presumed.

operations.coupling: Return exactly $m$ selected coordinate values, from which total loss is computable; unselected coordinates remain hidden. operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

public_inputs: Public nonempty action set $\mathcal X$; each action activates exactly $m$ coordinates.
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.
source_fields.query_domain_description: The public action set $\mathcal X\subseteq\{0,1\}^d$ is nonempty, and every action satisfies $\|a\|_1=m$.

source_fields.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.

source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Single-round action losses lie in $[0,m]$, so cumulative external regret lies in $[-mT,mT]$.

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
One semi-bandit event per round supplies $m$ scalars: $T$ rounds and $mT$ observed coordinates in total.
Exactly m active coordinates are observed each round, for mT in total.
OSMD updates once per round over the convex hull of the action set. Arbitrary internal computation is permitted.

source_fields.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
source_fields.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.
source_fields.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
source_fields.online_cost: Algorithms may depend on the public action set $\mathcal X$ and need not run in polynomial time. OSMD updates in $\operatorname{conv}(\mathcal X)$ and randomizes over actions. The feedback bound does not certify efficient implementation for arbitrary $\mathcal X$.
source_fields.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
source_fields.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real internal computation is allowed, with algorithm families depending on the public action set and no polynomial-time restriction. OSMD updates over the convex hull and implements randomized actions. Efficiency of these operations for an arbitrary action set is not guaranteed by the feedback bound.
source_fields.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.

source_fields.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A(\mathcal X)}\sup_{\varnothing\ne\mathcal X}\sup_{z_{1:T}\in([0,1]^d)^T}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: The learner is an algorithm family taking the public action set 𝒳 as input.
Take the infimum over these algorithm families, then the supremum over nonempty public action sets X satisfying the cardinality constraint.
With $\mathcal X$ fixed, take the supremum over oblivious coordinate-loss sequences. Expectation includes only learner randomness.
The comparator is the best fixed action in X in hindsight, not an arbitrary combination changing each round.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
source_fields.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.

source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

description_paragraphs: Each round, the learner selects an allowed combination, incurs the sum of its coordinate losses, and observes each selected coordinate separately. The upper bound holds for every admissible action set. The lower bound requires a specified hard action set and does not apply to singleton action sets.

description_paragraphs: The public combinatorial action set $\mathcal{X}$ is nonempty, and every action activates m coordinates. The minimax quantity takes the worst case over public action sets; it does not assert equal hardness for every fixed combinatorial geometry.
The hidden coordinate-loss vector is $z_t$, with each coordinate in [0,1], so total action loss lies in [0,m].
The selected combinatorial action $a_t$ must belong to $\mathcal{X}$. The m selected coordinates are observed.
Require $d\ge1$, $1\le m\le d/2$, and $T\ge1$. Dimension and horizon windows with matching bounds are specified in their respective regions.
The per-round loss is a sum over coordinates, without division by $m$.
